With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Coquitlam East

items.t: Established east-side house lots: single-detached streets under the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 (Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996), with a much thinner strata segment than the city average. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character from the zones, as the City states it: minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2; the SSMUH unit counts turn on the 280 m² and 4,050 m² thresholds.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam's SSMUH framework expressly leaves lots not connected to municipal water or sewer outside the SSMUH rules — the City's own servicing qualifier for house lots here — and Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste.

Watercourse character — the 50-metre Northeast rule: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam, and within 30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam — which side of that line a Coquitlam East lot sits on is a parcel check, and creek- and ravine-edge lots carry permit diligence.
ALR status is a property-specific check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Market context, labelled correctly: Coquitlam is a SnapStats-covered community; SnapStats has no land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: Coquitlam East sub-area detached inventory 28 / sales 4 (14%) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 9 / 1 (11%); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $625,000.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam East

items.t: Coquitlam East is the established east side of the City of Coquitlam, around David Avenue, Coast Meridian Road and the Eagle Ridge / Lansdowne Drive slopes below Burke Mountain. "Coquitlam East" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.
Main roads: Lougheed Highway, David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road serve east Coquitlam.

Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the west, Burke Mountain / Northeast Coquitlam (Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek, Partington Creek) to the north-east, Port Coquitlam across the Coquitlam River to the east, and Port Moody to the west.
Transit: Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express), at Lougheed Highway and Pinetree Way, is the main station for east Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam East

items.t: The watercourse setback doubles at an invisible line: 50 metres from the top of bank in Northeast Coquitlam versus 30 metres in the rest of the city — two otherwise similar east-side lots can carry materially different buildable envelopes purely on which side of the Northeast Coquitlam line they sit, and no City plan boundary for "Coquitlam East" itself is published to settle it from the street.

A "Not allowed" rental line from 2019 is void law today: the 455 Bromley Street feature sheet's "Pet/Rental: Not allowed" line predates November 24, 2022, when every BC strata long-term rental-restriction bylaw became void.

Coquitlam East is the established east side of the City of Coquitlam, around David Avenue, Coast Meridian Road and the Eagle Ridge and Lansdowne Drive slopes below Burke Mountain.
"Eagle Ridge" and "Lansdowne" are the local names used on these streets, while "Coquitlam East" is the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR) sub-area name.
The stock is mainly single-detached houses on the east-side streets, with a much thinner strata segment than the City Centre side of Coquitlam.
The school cluster is the area's built landmark set: Eagle Ridge Elementary at 1215 Falcon Drive, Scott Creek Middle at 1240 Lansdowne Drive and Gleneagle Secondary at 1195 Lansdowne Drive.

blocks.text: Coquitlam East: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The east-side difference is the watercourse permit distance: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam, against 30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam.

The Northeast Coquitlam neighbourhood plans (Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek, Partington Creek) cover the city's north-east, not this established sub-area; no Coquitlam East neighbourhood plan was confirmed.

blocks.text: Coquitlam East: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Three SD43 schools stand within the sub-area's streets: Eagle Ridge Elementary, 1215 Falcon Drive; Scott Creek Middle, 1240 Lansdowne Drive; Gleneagle Secondary, 1195 Lansdowne Drive.
David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road are the east-west and north-south spines; Lougheed Highway is the southern through-route to Coquitlam Central Station.
City Centre recreation — the City Centre Aquatic Complex and Town Centre Park — sits west of the sub-area in the City Centre, not inside Coquitlam East.
Coquitlam Public Library's City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, and Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, serve the city, with the Library Link mobile service.

blocks.text: Coquitlam East: development and new projects

items.t: Growth planning touching this area is the Northeast Coquitlam work — the Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek neighbourhood plans and the Northwest Burke Vision — which applies north-east of the established streets, named here once.
Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express), at Lougheed Highway and Pinetree Way, is the rapid-transit door for the east side.
David Avenue runs the length of the sub-area's north side toward Burke Mountain; Coast Meridian Road links it south to Lougheed Highway and east-side Port Coquitlam routes.

blocks.text: Coquitlam East: risks and due diligence

items.t: Apply the 50-metre Northeast Coquitlam watercourse permit distance, not the 30-metre city standard, when a lot sits near a creek on the sub-area's north-east edge — confirm which side of that line the parcel falls on with the City.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Coquitlam East?
faq.a: No known one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering is known. Land trades as built house lots on the east-side streets and the thin Atlin Place / Bromley strata segment.

faq.q: Can a Coquitlam East house lot add units?
faq.a: Yes under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage / laneway homes — but lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the rules, so confirm services and the exact zone (R-1 / R-2 / R-3) before advertising unit potential.

faq.q: Are the Lansdowne Drive townhomes Coquitlam East or Eagle Ridge?
faq.a: Search both sub-area names or you will miss listings either way.

faq.q: Is a Coquitlam East lot serviced?
faq.a: The City's framework assumes municipal water and sewer for SSMUH eligibility and bills water, sewer/drainage and solid waste as City utilities.

faq.q: What servicing bylaw governs a subdivision here?
faq.a: The Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — works and services to the City's standards under that bylaw, including owner-granted statutory rights-of-way and owner-paid City signage, confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Lansdowne Drive address?
faq.a: Gleneagle Secondary is itself at 1195 Lansdowne Drive and Scott Creek Middle at 1240 Lansdowne Drive, so this catchment cluster sits inside the neighbourhood; School District No. 43 (SD43) catchments are still address-based, so run the exact house address in the locator.

faq.q: Does the Burke Mountain plan cover my lot?
faq.a: Not automatically. The Northeast Coquitlam neighbourhood plans — Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek — cover the north-east part of the city above this sub-area, and no Coquitlam East plan was confirmed in City sources. A lot's permissions come from its zoning, its development permit areas and the city-wide Official Community Plan (OCP), not from a Burke Mountain plan name.

faq.q: Why does the creek setback differ on the east side?
faq.a: Because the City sets a wider permit area in the north-east. The Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area reaches 50 metres from the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam, versus 30 metres elsewhere in Coquitlam, and Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 sections 519 and 523 add flood and riparian setbacks. Ravine lots here need the permit check earlier, not later.

faq.q: Which station do east-side residents use?
faq.a: Coquitlam Central Station is the main station for east Coquitlam, on the Millennium Line (Evergreen Extension) at Lougheed Highway and Pinetree Way, and it also carries West Coast Express service.
Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) is the main station for east Coquitlam, and it also has West Coast Express service.
